content_preview.title: Codex CLI 0.163.0 Adds /config Search, Mid-Turn Steering and a /keymap Leader Key, and Checks Permission Before Proxy DNS Lookups
content_preview.summary: OpenAI's Codex CLI 0.163.0 adds a searchable /config, follow-up steering during a response, a configurable leader key and parallel read-only tools, plus network proxy and thread-resume permission fixes.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

OpenAI's Codex command-line coding agent has a new stable release. Version 0.163.0 was published on October 15, according to its [GitHub release page](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.163.0), and the project's [releases listing](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases) marks it as the latest stable release. The notes combine interface changes, a permission-related change to the network proxy, and a change to how the agent handles shells and tools. The Machine He...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured Briefing (711 words, within the 300-800 range; title 129 chars). Faithfully organized by the release notes' own sections (New Features, Bug Fixes, Documentation, Chores). Appropriate hedging: the article states that the notes do not describe Daybreak, do not link the proxy/permission fixes to any advisory or CVE, and do not quantify package-size or parallel-tool effects.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read manifest.json and both gzipped snapshots (source-0.html.gz = release page rust-v0.163.0, source-1.html.gz = releases listing); both status 200, suspicious_patterns null for both. Because summarizing fetchers have returned bogus release years for this page, I did not rely on any summarizer: I cross-checked against the raw GitHub API (gh api repos/openai/codex/releases/tags/rust-v0.163.0 and the releases list). source-0 (release page): the raw notes confirm all six New Features (searchable /config; follow-up steering plus interrupt stopping Code Mode cells and nested tool calls; /keymap leader key, default Ctrl+X, hints stay open, voice mute to F9; /daemon restart with warning and automatic reconnect; parallel read-only tools incl. skill, memory, conversation-history lookups; Daybreak enabled by default for eligible accounts, codex exec selectable with an OpenAI API key when the server offers access). All direct quotes verified verbatim against the raw notes (including 'Open `/config` to search preferences across categories, change supported settings immediately, and see which changes require a restart.', 'Send a follow-up while Codex is responding to steer it immediately.', 'Configure a leader key in `/keymap`.', 'Codex can run independent read-only tools in parallel, including skill, memory, and conversation-history lookups.', 'Daybreak is enabled by default for eligible accounts', 'The network proxy now checks permission before a DNS lookup, rejects duplicate `Host` headers, and prevents credential aliases from bypassing inspection hooks.', 'restores its permissions and network approvals, while respecting explicit overrides and current managed policy', 'Clarified how the Linux sandbox uses bubblewrap for filesystem isolation and seccomp for syscall filtering.', 'Codex now uses its standard shell executor and no longer bundles a patched `zsh`'). Remaining bug-fix bullets (/side, Windows/WSL paste, local/remote command output, codex exec duplicate diff), Documentation (GPT-6 family migration guidance) and Chores (retired shell flags migration notice; symbol stripping for Linux/macOS packages with symbols preserved in original build outputs) match the notes. Each item belongs to the 0.163.0 notes (changelog compares rust-v0.162.0...rust-v0.163.0); none is wrongly attributed to an alpha or an earlier release. Date: API published_at is 2026-10-15T21:30:38Z (created 2026-10-15T18:57:08Z), the snapshot datetime matches; 'October 15' confirmed, prerelease=false, draft=false. source-1 (releases listing): GitHub API releases/latest returns rust-v0.163.0 and the snapshot shows the 'Latest' label; 0.164.0-alpha.1 (2026-10-16T14:49:55Z), alpha.2 (2026-10-16T17:37:51Z) and alpha.3 (2026-10-17T04:03:25Z) are the only 0.164.0 entries, all prereleases, so 'pre-releases published on October 16 and 17' and 'no stable 0.164.0' are accurate. The snapshots are the canonical content; the live API was used only as a cross-check and agrees with them.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every feature, fix, default key (Ctrl+X, F9), and date verified individually. No contributor credits or personal names are asserted in the body (PR numbers and @handles in the notes' Changelog section are not used), so no credit risk. Minor framing nit, not worth a correction: the body lists '/side' under other fixes as 'A `/side` command to return to an existing side conversation'; the notes say 'Return to an existing side conversation with `/side` after switching threads' (a Bug Fixes bullet; changelog #52184 'Preserve side conversations across thread navigation'). The wording is slightly ambiguous about whether the command is new but it is filed under fixes, so it does not materially mislead. The Analysis sentence about a pattern in recent Codex versions is consistent with the prior 0.162.0 article's sandbox content and is appropriately caveated.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and descriptive. Subject is OpenAI, a competitor of Anthropic, whose Claude model powers this newsroom; I checked specifically for competitor disparagement or favorable spin. The article attributes everything to OpenAI's own release notes, uses no evaluative language, states the absence of any advisory or CVE, and makes no comparison with Claude Code or other tools. Neutral treatment confirmed; no conflict-of-interest concern affects the verdict.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. The only prior Codex CLI release article is 2026-10/09 (0.162.0, worktree tools); no coverage of 0.163.0 exists in src/content/articles. The article links the prior piece with the correct singular form /article/2026-10/09-codex-cli-01620-adds-managed-git-worktree-tools-and-tightens-linux-sandbox-handling-of-ripgrep-config-and-writable-executables, which matches an existing file in src/content/articles/2026-10/ and so resolves. Orphan-link diff: body external URLs are exactly the two in article.sources (release tag page, releases listing); the only other link is the internal article link; no orphans in either direction.
recommendations: In future, phrase the /side item as a behavior fix (e.g. returning to an existing side conversation with /side after switching threads) to avoid implying a new command.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, accurate, well-hedged first-party release briefing. All claims, quotes, dates and release attributions verified against the raw GitHub release notes and API. github.com is already allowlisted. APPROVE.
